newsitem.title: INDIA: Erratic rains to cut India's 96/97 coffee output.
newsitem.headline: Erratic rains to cut India's 96/97 coffee output.

text.p: India's coffee output in 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) is expected to fall sharply below target due to unseasonal rains in the past two months, planters and industry officials said on Tuesday.

"Kodagu, Chickmagalur and Hassan districts in (the southern state of) Karnataka, which accounts for 70 percent of the country's coffee production, received heavy rains several times in the last two months," said Appaya, a leading planter.
"(Due to this) our crop has been damaged heavily," he said.
India's state-run Coffee Board in November set a coffee output target of 205,000 tonnes for 1996/97, including 89,950 tonnes of arabica and 115,050 tonnes of robusta.
Industry sources, prior to the November rains, had estimated the 1996/97 output at around 180,000 tonnes.
"Although it is too early to predict the exact damage, it is clear that there will be a sharp decline over the industry's estimate (after the rains)," said one coffee trader.
Planters estimate the 1995/96 coffee crop at around 200,000 tonnes.
M. Venkatesh, president of the Coffee Federation of India said that coffee worth 1,100 million rupees had been damaged due to recent rains.
Planters said the unseasonal rains in the last two months would also affect the 1997/98 coffee crop.
"The unseasonal rains had led to withering of leaves to prevent the formation of buds next year," said Jagannath, a leading planter.
"Yellow rust disease has also affected the crop," he said.
Planters said they have sought tax concessions from the Karnataka government on exports in view of the losses suffered due to crop damage.
"Without this, exporters cannot operate," said a leading exporter.
